Health Data Analyst · ML/AI · Computer Vision

Chayanika Devi

I am a health data analyst and machine learning researcher focused on digital health and computer vision. I analyze population and surveillance data to build interactive dashboards and maps that identify gaps in healthcare access. In computer vision, I work with stereo and infrared camera systems, calibrating them for six-degrees-of-freedom (6DoF) pose estimation in neurosurgical navigation research. My core tools include Python, PyTorch, OpenCV, and GIS.

About

Chayanika
Devi

I am a health data researcher based in Honolulu, Hawaiʻi, working where public health, data science, and computer vision meet. Most analysts specialize in one area. I bring three together: epidemiology and GIS to find where care is missing, machine learning and dashboards to turn complex data into clear decisions, and computer vision to support clinical tools such as neurosurgical navigation.

With 3+ years of research across the US and international teams, publications in BMJ Global Health and Frontiers in Digital Health, and national presentations at the American Association of Neurological Surgeons (AANS) and the American Association of Geographers (AAG), I bring rigor, curiosity, and clear communication to every team I join, with a lasting commitment to more equitable healthcare.

Space-Time Clusters of COVID-19 in Rural and Urban U.S. Counties

My M.S. thesis at the University of Cincinnati. Detected county-level COVID-19 space-time clusters across the U.S. over 105 weeks and compared how rural and urban counties were affected in each phase of the pandemic.

Computer Vision Projects

Camera calibration, pose estimation, and medical imaging for neurosurgical navigation.

Jan 2026 – May 2026

6DoF Head Pose Tracking Using OptiTrack and Stereo Camera

Calibrated a 6-camera system (4 OptiTrack Prime 13/13W IR cameras + ZED 2i) with ChArUco boards over 2 trials of up to 300 frames, reaching 0.17 px RMS reprojection error. Identified IR-filter incompatibility with paper boards and proposed reflective marker boards.

OpenCVZED SDKOptiTrackPython
Learn more
May 2025 – Jul 2025

Computer Vision Based Calibration Using a Pixel Phone Camera

Computed intrinsic camera parameters from ChArUco images (1920 × 1080 px) for pose estimation, and evaluated accuracy by comparing reprojection error across board orientations and lighting conditions.

OpenCVCamera calibrationPython
Learn more
Mar 2025 – May 2025

Low-Cost Open-Source Image-Guided Navigation for Skull Models

Configured SlicerIGT in 3D Slicer with freehand calibration (fCal) and a built-in webcam for real-time pose tracking, demonstrating a proof-of-concept neuronavigation workflow on a 3D skull model.

3D SlicerSlicerIGTfCalPlus Server
Learn more
Jan 2025 – Feb 2025

Open-Source Medical Image Processing with Python

Built a CT/MRI loading and visualization pipeline using 3D Slicer's Python interpreter and Jupyter, with interactive widgets for real-time 2D/3D rendering and segmentation via SlicerJupyter.

Jupyter3D SlicerDICOM
Learn more
Oct 2024 – Dec 2024

AI-Based Medical Image Segmentation Using MONAI Label

Explored MONAI Label and NVIDIA AIAA within 3D Slicer to perform AI-assisted 3D segmentation on MRI datasets for neurosurgical planning.

MONAINVIDIA AIAAMRI
